newsitem.title: UK: Crashed Saudi 747 hull insured for $36mln - sources.
newsitem.headline: Crashed Saudi 747 hull insured for $36mln - sources.

text.p: The hull of the Saudi Airlines Boeing 747 which crashed near New Delhi on Tuesday was insured for $36 million, according to insurance market sources.
Cover for the airliner, which collided with a Kazakhstan airliner in mid-air at around 1330 GMT, had been placed by a consortium of insurance brokers CT Bowring and Willis Corroon.
The lead insurer was the Aerial syndicate at Lloyd's of London, and market sources said the bulk of the claim for the airliner' hull was likely to land on the London insurance market.

Initial reports are still unclear, and a second industry source suggested that the hull insurance could be even higher. He added that international insurance markets outside London were also likely to be involved.
The figure for passenger liability, likely to be more than the hull value, was not available. The final figure will depend largely on the profiles of the passengers.
Nearly 350 people are feared dead in what may be the worst air disaster ever.

Insurers are still trying to identify the second airliner involved. Initial reports said it was a Kazakh Airways TU-154. The airline does not usually fly the route on which the crash happened, but experts say the aircraft could have been chartered to another airline.
